examples.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Quotient Containing Other Functions

feedback.worked_solution:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x)=6x$ and $v(x)=1-3x,$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(x) & =6, \\ {v}^{′}(x) & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot (1-3x)-6x\cdot (-3)}{{(1-3x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6-18x+18x}{{(1-3x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{{(1-3x)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
